answer: Require each agent to lock a refundable deposit released only after it completes verifiable work, so creating thousands of fake identities becomes expensive rather than free. Like a wharf charging every ship that docks, the system collects a small bond per identity and slashes it for fraud. Honest agents instead build a public signal over time — completed jobs, satisfied counterparties, and uptime that cannot be faked overnight, like a meadow growing slowly rather than appearing instantly. An attacker must pay real cost for every fake, while legitimate agents reuse one trusted identity.
